subject: Re: Trial burst credits requested for inference load validation
messages:
From: Taylor Jordan <taylor.jordan@acmecorp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: short burst of trial credits for heavy load POC

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The engineering team is ready to run a concentrated throughput/latency validation of Redwood on our real prompts next Tuesday. The tests will run for ~6 hours and simulate sustained concurrent connections (400 parallel sessions, avg. 120 tokens/resp) to validate tail latency and batching behavior.

Can Redwood provision a short-term trial boost (credits or quota increase) to cover ~12M tokens so we don't hit limits during the run? We can share the signed data handling addendum and the test plan (attached).

Appreciate a quick confirmation — we want to lock the window and coordinate our infra.

Thanks,
Taylor Jordan
Staff SRE, Acme Corp
(taylor.jordan@acmecorp.com)

Attachment: ACME_POCTestPlan_v3.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Taylor Jordan <taylor.jordan@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short burst of trial credits for heavy load POC

Hi Taylor —

Thanks for the plan and the details, that level of context helps. Before we provision anything, two quick asks so Diego (sales ops) and Marcus (infra) can sign off:

- Confirm expected peak RPS and whether traffic is evenly distributed or bursty.
- Confirm whether you need separate private routing (dedicated pool) or the hosted quota increase is fine.
- Copy of signed DPA/ADD and the NDA (I see one attached).

As for numbers: 12M tokens should be fine as a one-off promo if the team is comfortable with the test constraints. We typically grant a timed "burst credit" tied to a PO/HubSpot record and a start/end window; Diego will set the amount and internal billing note. Marcus will advise on soft limits so your test doesn't trigger automatic throttles.

Looping in: Diego Fernandez (account lead) and Marcus Lin (serving infra) — can you review and propose an approved credit amount and any routing/soft-limit guidance?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | (650) 555-0184

Quoted from original:> Attachment: ACME_POCTestPlan_v3.pdf

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Taylor Jordan <taylor.jordan@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-02T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short burst of trial credits for heavy load POC

Thanks for the context, all. Per our promotional guidelines and ACME's engagement level (HS-234567), I'm prepared to approve a one-time credit top-up to cover 12,000,000 tokens for a 48-hour scheduled window. I'll attach the billing note to the HubSpot deal and tag this as promotional POC support.

Notes / constraints for the ACME engineers:
- The credit will be active from 2026-08-09T08:00:00-07:00 to 2026-08-11T08:00:00-07:00 (48h). Please confirm if you need a different window.
- We'll keep a soft RPS throttle at 500 rps cluster-wide; sustained higher RPS may be subject to throttling for safety.
- If you need dedicated capacity (no throttles) we can discuss a short-term dedicated reservation, but that requires an escalation and formal commit.

Marcus, any infra caveats to add?

Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.ai

Attachment: NDA_signed_ACME.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Taylor Jordan <taylor.jordan@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short burst of trial credits for heavy load POC

Hi folks — quick infra notes to make the test go smoothly:

- We'll provision the 12M tokens as Diego outlined and attach an operational flag to the ACME project so we can observe the run in realtime.
- Please use the test API key that Soojin will provision; do not run tests from a production key.
- Keep average prompt length and response length consistent with your plan; sudden spikes in prompt size can make batching less effective and increase tail latency.
- If you expect sustained >400 concurrent sessions, notify us 48h before start so we can raise soft throttles temporarily.

Soojin — I can provision the credits and create the test API key if you confirm the start window. Taylor — confirm the dates and we will mark the HubSpot record.

— Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
